newsletter.subject: Selmara Glacier's retreat speeds up
newsletter.text:
## This week

A survey team from the University of Norvale found that the Selmara Glacier retreated 410 meters over the past year, the fastest pace since measurements began in 1962. The previous record was 260 meters.

The team, led by glaciologist Petra Lindqvar, used drone mapping and 14 ground stations. They found the glacier's surface dropped by an average of 3.1 meters, and that meltwater lakes on its surface doubled in number to 48.

Downstream, the town of Esker Bay relies on the glacier's meltwater for about 40% of its summer drinking water. The town council voted last week to fund a new reservoir costing $18 million, due to open in 2029.

Lindqvar said the team will publish the full data set in January and repeat the survey every six months instead of every year.
